matches.rationale: No finding addresses the abstract's overstated claim about 'even improve performance' without sufficient qualification. Finding 1 concerns Proposition 2 unbiasedness, Finding 2 concerns uncited references, and Finding 3 concerns Appendix B.2 importance sampling—none relate to the abstract's performance claim.

No finding identifies the Introduction's citation of future publications (2024, 2025) as established works. Finding 2 mentions uncited references but does not address citing future/speculative work as settled findings.
No finding flags the incorrect closed-form formula in Proposition 1 missing normalization (softmax). Finding 3 discusses importance sampling in Appendix B.2, which is a different mathematical issue.
No finding mentions the omission of data augmentation details (flips, crops) in the experimental section. None of the three findings address experimental design protocols.
No finding identifies the truncation/rescaling of memorization metrics or omitted error bars in Figure 2. Findings cover unrelated issues.

Both the ground truth and Finding 1 target the unbiasedness claim associated with Proposition 2. The GT describes a corruption where the estimator is incorrectly claimed to be unbiased, while Finding 1 observes an internal contradiction between the text (claiming approximate unbiasedness) and Proposition 2 (claiming exact unbiasedness). Both identify the same scientific issue—the unbiasedness claim is problematic—at the same location.
No finding addresses the marketing-style phrasing ('consistent modest but steady improvements') in the description of Figure 4. This rhetorical issue is not captured by any of the three findings.

No finding identifies the contradiction between the Conclusion's overstatement of contributions and the Limitations section's admission of unexplored factors. The three findings do not cover conclusion/limitations misalignment.
No finding discusses the omitted privacy risk discussion or lack of mitigation strategies in the broader impact section. None of the findings address ethical integrity omissions.
No finding addresses the understated computational overhead of M additional samples in the Method section. The findings are unrelated to computational efficiency claims.
No finding covers the omission of M > 1000 results or the 'nearly identical' claims. The evidence data integrity issue about unreported larger M values is not among the findings.
No finding identifies promotional language ('remarkable agreement,' 'clearly answers') in the Related Work section. This rhetorical manipulation is not captured by any finding.
No finding addresses the contradictory narratives about stochasticity's role between Section 3.1 and earlier sections. This cross-section inconsistency is not identified in any of the three findings.
